name: Carol S. Dweck
person: Carol S. Dweck, Stanford psychologist, author of "Mindset: The New Psychology of Success," creator of growth-mindset theory (fixed vs. growth mindset). NOT any other Carol Dweck.

enumPrompts.label: ensaios-talks
enumPrompts.prompt:
Enumerate PRIMARY content from {{PERSON}} beyond what's already known (the Mindset book, TED talk, HBR articles 2014/2016, Education Week 2015 revisit essay, "Even Geniuses Work Hard" essay, several academic papers with Yeager/Mueller/Canning co-authors).
1. Walk Stanford's own faculty pages, her lab site (mindsetscholarsnetwork.org if it exists, or Stanford SPARQ), and Google Scholar for any additional first-person essay, op-ed, or long-form written piece not yet cited, especially anything addressing the 2018-2023 replication-crisis controversy directly in her own words.
2. Find any additional academic papers with substantial first-person theoretical framing (not just abstracts), particularly ones where she personally responds to critics (Sisk et al., Macnamara & Burgoyne) in her own voice.
3. Any book excerpt, foreword, or updated-edition preface where she reflects on how "growth mindset" was popularized/commercialized beyond her original intent (the "false growth mindset" concern is already cited once, find more depth on this).
Return exact URLs, priority=high for anything with substantial first-person content, one-line "why" per item.

enumPrompts.label: entrevistas-recentes
enumPrompts.prompt:
Enumerate INTERVIEW/PODCAST appearances of {{PERSON}} beyond the ones already known (KQED MindShift "false growth mindset" interview, Tes Magazine interview on critics).
1. Any long-form podcast/interview appearance (academic, business, or education-focused) where she discusses her own research career, how she arrived at mindset theory from earlier work on learned helplessness, her mentors/influences.
2. Any interview specifically addressing the replication-crisis pushback on growth mindset research, her own point-by-point response to specific meta-analyses, not just general defenses.
3. Any interview about how growth mindset got applied/misapplied in corporate and education settings, her own critique of the "corporate mindset industry" that grew around her work.
Return exact URLs, priority-marked, 6-10 items with transcripts preferred.

enumPrompts.label: criticas
enumPrompts.prompt:
Enumerate CRITIQUES and adversarial material on {{PERSON}} and growth-mindset theory beyond what's already known (Sisk et al. 2018 meta-analysis, Macnamara & Burgoyne 2023 meta-analysis, the KQED "dueling meta-analyses" piece).
1. Named academic critics beyond Sisk/Macnamara/Burgoyne, any psychologist or education researcher who has published direct methodological critique of Dweck's original studies (small effect sizes, non-replication, the "growth mindset industry" critique).
2. Critiques of the commercial/corporate application of growth mindset, consultants, HR critics, or journalists who've argued the theory got oversimplified or weaponized in ways she didn't intend.
3. Any critique specifically of the 2019 Yeager/Dweck "National Study of Learning Mindsets", statisticians or education researchers who've challenged its methodology or interpretation.
Return exact URLs, type=critique, 6-10 items, this is an academic controversy, prioritize named researchers with published critique over journalistic hot-takes.
